wu: Students play 'Two Truths and a Lie' about their week, writing three sentences on paper (two true, one false) and guessing which is false. They say 'I went to the market' or 'I watched a movie' to practice past simple.
wuAlt: Students draw a quick picture of their week and label it in English, sharing with a partner
Students ask 'Did you...?' questions about weekend activities (e.g., 'Did you cook?')
pres: Show a PET listening task on the board (Part 1: short conversations). Model predicting answers by looking at the question options and circling keywords. Play a sample audio and demonstrate note-taking with symbols (✔/✗, arrows). Check understanding by asking 'What do we listen for first?'
presAlt: Use a transcript with blanks to show how keywords help fill gaps
Play a short audio without questions and ask students to jot down key words
prac: Students work in pairs to predict answers for a PET Part 1 task, then listen and check. They use a table to mark 'Predicted' vs 'Heard'. Support with keyword flashcards (e.g., 'appointment', 'library').
pracAlt: Students match question types to listening strategies (e.g., 'When?' = time words)
ls: Students complete a PET Part 2 multiple-choice monologue task. They first predict answers, listen once to check, then listen again to take notes. They compare notes in pairs before final answers.
re: Students stand and play 'Simon Says' with listening commands (e.g., 'Simon says touch your ear if you heard 'library'').
prod: Students roleplay a job interview, using note-taking to remember questions. One student asks 'Why should we hire you?' and the other answers with past experiences, then reports notes to a partner.
rw: Students read a short article about 'Finding a Job in Oujda' and answer inference questions (e.g., 'Why is it hard to find work?'). They then write a 80-word email applying for a job using past experiences.
st: Play a short video about 'Workplace Skills' and discuss. Close with 'Today we practiced PET listening strategies—good job! Thank you, class.'
g: Students match question types to listening keywords (e.g., 'Where?' to 'place')
Students listen to a short audio and race to write 3 key words
Students mark predicted answers on a grid and cross off when heard
Teams take turns doing job interview roleplays with notes
Students find mistakes in a transcript and explain why
diff: Fast finishers: Write a new PET listening task for the class
Support: Use a partially filled note-taking template
hw: Complete a PET listening Part 3 task online and record your score
Listen to a podcast and write 5 notes about main points
Write a 100-word review of a movie using past tenses
tip: Encourage students to use Arabic to clarify predictions, then switch to English for note-taking—this builds confidence while targeting exam skills.
